data.name: Constantin
data.gender_notes: Constantin is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Konstantinos, which means 'infant of Constantine'. Constantine the Great was a Roman emperor who converted the Roman Empire to Christianity. The name Constantin carries the meaning “Firm, constant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Constantin usually hope their child will grow to embody firm, constant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Constantin belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Firm, constant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Constantin total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Constantin represents the historical figure of Emperor Constantine the Great, who not only united the Roman Empire but also played a significant role in the spread of Christianity. His reign marked the beginning of the Christian Roman Empire, and his actions paved the way for Christianity to become the dominant religion in Europe.
data.spiritual_significance: Constantin holds a deep spiritual significance for Christians as he is remembered as the emperor who granted religious tolerance and even made Christianity legal within the Roman Empire. His conversion to Christianity and his subsequent influence on the empire led to a greater acceptance and spread of the faith, making him a revered figure in Christian history.
